records.text: Civil Appeal No. 57 of 1951 arises from a judgment of the High Court of East Punjab affirming a single judge's decision dismissing objections under Section 47 of the Civil Procedure Code regarding execution of a money decree.
records.event: Filing of Civil Appeal challenging execution proceedings
records.procedure: Civil Appeal before Supreme Court; prior proceedings in High Court of East Punjab and Subordinate Judge, Ambala

records.text: On September 30, 1925, Baldev Das, manager of a joint Hindu family, executed a mortgage bond in favor of Mst. Naraini for Rs 16,000 using joint family movable properties as security.
records.event: Execution of mortgage bond for loan

records.text: On April 16, 1928, the appellants (sons) filed a partition suit against their father Baldev Das, resulting in a final decree dividing joint family properties by metes and bounds on July 20, 1928.
records.event: Partition suit filed and decree passed
records.procedure: Suit No. 23 of 1928 in Court of Subordinate Judge, Shahjahanpur

records.text: On September 29, 1934, Mst. Naraini filed a suit against Baldev Das for recovery of Rs 12,500 based on the 1925 mortgage bond, claiming against both mortgaged property and joint family assets.
records.event: Recovery suit filed by mortgagee
records.procedure: Suit in Court of Senior Subordinate Judge, Ambala

records.text: On December 18, 1934, appellants applied to be added as defendants to the recovery suit, asserting that properties were partitioned and allotted to them, not liable for father's debt.
records.event: Application to add appellants as parties to suit
records.procedure: Proceedings in Senior Subordinate Judge, Ambala

records.text: Plaintiff's counsel abandoned claim against mortgaged property on February 7, 1935, seeking only a money decree against Baldev Das personally; appellants withdrew application to be added as parties.
records.event: Amendment of plaint and withdrawal of application

records.text: On April 17, 1935, Baldev Das died; on September 2, appellants and their mother were brought on record as legal representatives of Baldev Das.
records.event: Death of Baldev Das and substitution of parties

records.text: On November 20, 1935, parties compromised; a money decree was passed against Baldev Das's estate in hands of legal representatives for Rs 425 annas odd plus half costs.
records.event: Compromise and passing of money decree

records.text: On March 13, 1945, decree holder filed execution application; court attached immovable properties (shops) in possession of appellants at Abdullaput.
records.event: Execution application filed and attachment of properties
records.procedure: Execution Case No. 18 of 1945; Senior Subordinate Judge, Ambala

records.text: On April 23, 1945, appellants filed objections under Section 47, arguing attached properties were their separate post-partition shares and not liable for father's pre-partition debt.
records.event: Filing of objections under Section 47 CPC
records.procedure: Execution Case No. 18 of 1945; Senior Subordinate Judge, Ambala

records.text: Subordinate Judge held partition occurred in 1928; properties attached were allotted to sons; debt was pre-partition but not immoral; decreeholder entitled to execute against sons' shares under Hindu law and Section 53 CPC.
records.event: Judgment dismissing objections to execution based on Hindu law and CPC Section 53.
records.procedure: Execution proceedings in Senior Subordinate Judge, Ambala

records.text: High Court single judge (Rahman J.) dismissed appellants' appeal affirming Subordinate Judge; further appeal to Letters Patent Bench also dismissed; current appeal challenges Letters Patent Bench judgment.
records.event: Dismissal of appeals at High Court levels

records.text: Appellants contend decreeholder can proceed only against Baldev Das's estate per compromise terms; appellants' separate property cannot be made liable.
records.event: First contention raised in appeal

records.text: Second contention: post-partition separate property of sons is not liable under Hindu law for father's pre-partition debt.
records.event: Second contention raised in appeal

records.text: Third contention: if pious obligation exists, it must be enforced via proper suit, not execution of decree obtained against father alone when sons were added only as legal representatives post-death.
records.event: Third contention raised in appeal

records.text: No formal compromise petition filed; record contains two statements (one by appellant Pannalal, one by plaintiff's agent) setting out compromise terms matching decree wording.
records.event: Observation on absence of formal compromise petition

records.text: Argues 'estate of Baldev Das deceased' in decree refers only to property Baldev owned at death, excluding sons' post-partition shares where father had no interest.
records.event: Argument on interpretation of decree wording

limitations: The provided text is a summary of a legal case record and does not contain the full judgment or detailed reasoning of the Supreme Court regarding the final disposition of the appeal.
Specific dates for some procedural steps (e.g., exact date of High Court single judge's decision) are inferred from the narrative flow rather than explicitly stated in the provided snippets.
The text mentions 'half costs' but does not specify the exact amount beyond the principal decree amount of Rs. 425-7-0.
